key_concepts: Earth's plates move because of intense heat in Earth's core.
Molten rock in the asthenosphere flows due to heat from the core.
Convection currents form when warm material rises, cools, and sinks.
Plates have warmer, thinner parts that rise and colder, denser parts that sink.
New plate material rises at mid-ocean ridges and forms new crust.
Ridge push occurs when newly formed crust pushes the rest of the plate.
Old plate parts sink into the mantle at subduction zones.
Slab pull occurs when colder, thicker plate parts sink into the mantle.
Plate tectonic theory states that lithospheric plates move.
Convection currents in the mantle cause plates to diverge at mid-oceanic ridges.
The driving force for plate motion includes convection currents in the mantle.
The heat source from the core to the mantle is decayed radioactive elements.
